newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bund futures steady, profit-taking worry mounts.
newsitem.headline: Bund futures steady, profit-taking worry mounts.

text.p: German Bund futures had a difficult time building on their two-week long rally on Friday as traders grew nervous about profit-taking and M3 money supply data due next week which may not be Bund supportive.

Traders said the December Bund futures contract, which has climbed about 120 basis points so far this month, was starting to look vulnerable at above 101.00 and that the contract could fall if upcoming German data appeared to dispel speculation that the economy is growing only slowy.
At 1606 GMT, the December DTB Bund futures contract was up 0.05 basis points at 101.02 and down from a high of 101.14.
"The M3 figures could burt the bond market bubble," said Catherine Lee, bond market analyst at R.H. Wrightson & Associates.
She said that as Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing warned this morning, a flow of funds into the new Deutsche Telekom issue could inflate M3 money supply.
Even a one-off event, such as the Telekom float, could worry financial markets and trigger selling of Bunds, she said.
The Bund market will also have to keep an eye out for the German Ifo institute index next week which could give clues about the strength of economy.
Some analysts even figured there was a risk that M3 would not not fall below eight percent level from the 8.4 percent growth in posted in September.

Traders continued to see further flattening of the yield curve as speculation that the rate cycle has hit bottom gathered steam. The spread between five and 10 year notes narrowed to 122 basis points from 125 basis points on Friday.

Treasuries remained strong against Bunds, but could not break through the 40 basis point spread level. The spread stood at 43 basis points, down from 46 basis points at the previous close. --Frankfurt Newsroom +49 69 756525
